      "observations": [
        "All 10 owned paths and all 1,783 diff lines were read, including every changed test hunk. The port changes native count/select contracts, JS adapters and navigation counts, the public IDL, native helper placement and five test files. This is a functional asynchronous conversion, not a blanket formatting or bulk change.",
        "Counts become Promise APIs and selectMessages becomes a Promise for an array while still accepting limit/offset in this original phase. Both select methods now execute a storage callback rather than returning rows from ExecuteStep. The original selectMessagesInGroup already returned a Promise but populated it synchronously; this patch makes its query execution asynchronous too.",
        "Native CountMessagesListener retains a main-thread Promise handle, records an error string and stores the first count row. Selection owns a JS array, converts each storage result to message primitives and accumulates results until completion. CreateJSMessage helpers move from LiveView methods to namespace functions so the callback can use them; this is shared conversion code rather than a new message schema.",
        "The count listener declares mResult without an initializer and assigns it only if HandleResult receives a row. Its canceled/error branches invoke rejection but then still evaluate MaybeResolve(mResult). Selection's canceled/error paths instead return immediately after rejection, and JS-global initialization failure rejects and returns failure. Preserve this bounded count-versus-selection control-flow distinction; no failure injection, uninitialized-read reproduction or Promise-engine settlement audit was performed.",
        "The original LiveViewRowMap stops count work in its constructor. sortBy calls async resetRows without returning its promise. resetRows clears the cache, notifies removal, awaits count, resizes and notifies addition. rowAt must remain synchronous: it reserves empty TreeDataRow entries before starting a buffered select and returns a placeholder immediately. Array membership prevents another lookup from fetching the reserved interval again.",
        "When original row data arrives, its then continuation returns if the adapter was cleaned up, otherwise replaces placeholders and invalidates the requested range. cleanup clears the live listener/references/cache. There is no complete overlapping-sort/generation or rejection policy established by this scope; a successful rowAt return is not loaded data. The private helper is a custom rowAt API with documented non-negative indices, not Array.prototype.at.",
        "Original grouped and threaded top-level queries now update row count from then callbacks. Their sort callers do not expose the query-completion promise. The standalone document awaits unread and total counts sequentially in its existing loop; this does not mean all tree rows or visible pixels are ready.",
        "The SQL intentionally stops using ADDRESS_FORMAT for sender/recipients and aliases raw text instead. Tests comment out formatted sender/property/sort expectations rather than proving those features work. Preserve this admitted loss of formatting coverage; the shared UTF-8 producer and recipient-formatting lessons already cover the exact source boundary.",
        "Changed tests now await count/select results, while adapter tests first assert placeholder.message is undefined and then await invalidateRange before checking values. Buffer-from-top/bottom and insertion/removal scenarios remain sequential across date and subject orders. Group/thread tests await initial row counts and staged invalidations. These are direct assertions and event contracts, not executed results or coverage of cancellation/overlapping requests.",
        "The new ListenerTree helper and placeholder assertions contain missing messages: the rowCountChanged/invalidateRange state guards, promise-wait preconditions, expected index/delta/range assertions and several new strict undefined-message checks have no message. Existing property/emoji assertions also lack messages in the inspected scope. The helper's reset failure message does state should. No assertions or tests were edited by this study.",
        "Keep accepted architecture separate. LiveViewRowMap is retired. Accepted selectMessages has no pagination parameters, and results reach an adapter through inclusive onSelectedChunk callbacks. The native listener flushes the last chunk before resolving; the accepted base sort awaits countMessages and selectMessages. Exact accepted base/cleanup proof is reused unchanged from 4464. This is a later listener/streaming phase, not unchanged original lazy-cache behavior.",
        "Manual review covers actual native/JS receivers, async completion and cleanup, helper visibility, IDL comments, sparse placeholder membership, sequential awaits, listener waiters and assertion messages. The C++ callbacks have dense adjacent methods and nested result conversion; named conversion stages and blank-line groups would make ownership and completion easier to follow. This is a scoped readability suggestion, not a repository-wide rule. Paired storage callback, Promise and GC internals remain bounded unread.",
        "Exact full original Bug 1941471, current comments 0–51/activity/end controls, was reused by original ID and read from its retained rendered body. The shared meta spans earlier synchronous adapters, this async landing and later incremental/listener repairs; those later attachments and historical reports are separate phases, not newly audited dependency source.",
        "The meta's temporary read-only XPCOM-object proposal was made obsolete. Later incremental delivery explicitly reports knowingly breaking lower-priority behavior, followed by add/remove, ordering, cleanup and JSContext-lifetime work. Preserve that history without treating it as this patch's tested outcome or a proven root cause of the count callback observation.",
        "D272375's full creation-to-final timeline and all six submitted inline bodies were read. The author explains non-negative custom row lookup, renames at to rowAt and adds caller documentation; the owned source establishes [] lookup and the non-negative contract. This is not an Array.prototype.at equivalence claim or measured speed proof.",
        "The reviewer explicitly withdraws the entries-loop alternative because the separate i++ is useful here. The landed loop starts its output index at the requested buffer start; preserve this offset contract instead of turning the suggestion into an adopted style rule.",
        "The reviewer asks about only one pending request and the author says it may be fine and to see what happens. This does not establish an overlapping-query safeguard; later accepted cancellation is a separate source phase.",
        "BenC prefers a possible listener adapter for future native consumers but explicitly accepts Promises for current JS API exploration. The interface lands with Promises. Earlier acceptance, returning to WIP, the removed XPCOM parent, final two-reviewer acceptance and mixed remote-build events remain distinct historical steps, with no fresh execution."
